merged_from_phrasings: phone barely lasts half a day
battery goes from full to empty too fast
loses charge even when not in use
duplicate_issue_merges.rationale: All describe the same underlying complaint (excessive battery consumption during normal use) and share the same official Samsung remediation sequence (software update -> power saving -> background limits -> display tuning -> safe mode -> reset). Kept as ONE canonical_issue with 13 distinct atomic actions rather than one record per phrasing.

merged_from_phrasings: phone got slow after the update
phone became laggy after software update
apps started lagging after the update
duplicate_issue_merges.rationale: These are near-identical restatements of the same trigger (a recent software/One UI update) and share the same remediation path (settle/reboot -> wipe cache -> factory reset). NOT merged with the broader 'slow_device_general' issue, because the update-triggered path includes an update-specific step (wipe cache partition in recovery) that does not apply to general slowness with no update trigger.

Both 'no sound' and 'low volume' complaints are handled by the same official Samsung diagnostic sequence (Mute all sounds check -> Do not disturb -> balance -> accessory/Bluetooth check -> restart -> Safe Mode -> reset -> service). Kept together rather than split into two canonical issues since Samsung's own source articles do not separate them.

merged_from_phrasings: touch not working in some areas
duplicate_issue_merges.rationale: Partial dead-zone complaints and fully unresponsive-screen complaints share the same first-line Samsung troubleshooting steps (accessory check, restart, sensitivity setting, Safe Mode, diagnostics). Kept as one canonical_issue; the update-triggered variant was intentionally NOT merged in (see touch-009) because it has a distinct, less-verified remediation path and a different confidence rating.

Random drops and general instability are treated identically in Samsung's official Wi-Fi troubleshooting guide (TSG10002018). The 'Intelligent Wi-Fi auto-switching' variant (wifi-007) was NOT merged in because it has a distinct root cause (a specific software feature switching networks/data) and a lower-confidence, community-sourced fix.

explicit_not_merged_decisions.rationale: All are 'blurry/poor camera output' complaints on the surface, but the actual verified remediation differs by cause: lens cleaning/protector removal (general), minimum shooting distance (telephoto/high zoom, Ultra-model specific), expected optical softness (200MP mode, Ultra-model specific), condensation clearing (environmental/temporary), and OIS hardware damage (repair-only). Merging these would have hidden model-specific and severity-specific guidance the task explicitly asked to preserve.

Low storage is a documented CAUSE of app crashing (see app-004, S029), but the two are kept as separate canonical issues with cross-referenced actions rather than merged, since a user reporting 'storage almost full' is not necessarily also reporting app crashes, and vice versa.

Flicker while using the Camera app specifically has a distinct, documented root cause (lighting-frequency interaction with shutter speed, see disp-006/S008) unrelated to the general display-flicker troubleshooting path, so it was kept as its own canonical_issue rather than folded into general 'screen_flickering'. The Galaxy S26/S26+ specific guidance (disp-008/S010) was also kept separate because it is an official Samsung article scoped explicitly to those two models.

community_or_third_party_sourced_records.note: These records are NOT from official Samsung support pages. They are included because they represent commonly reported/plausible troubleshooting patterns, but should be weighted lower and ideally corroborated with an official source before being surfaced as a top-confidence fix.

unverified_or_partially_fetched_sources.note: These source URLs were identified (via search result snippets or as related-article links) but NOT independently fetched and fully verified in this research pass. Records citing them are marked confidence='low' or 'medium' and flagged in requires_human_review where appropriate.

sources_collected_but_not_cited_in_any_r.note: Fetched/identified during research but not directly used to source a specific troubleshooting record -- kept in sources.json for traceability and potential future use.

known_gaps.gap: No official Samsung source was found (within this research pass) giving an exact Settings path or deeplink-equivalent screen name for viewing charging speed/wattage in real time beyond 'Settings > Battery > remaining charging time'. Exact One UI menu wording for 'Fast charging' toggle by model/carrier was not independently verified.

'display_poor_resolution' records (disp-010/011/012) are based on a source (S046) that could not be fully fetched -- only referenced as a related-article link. Step content is inferred from general Samsung Settings conventions, not verified verbatim. Recommend a follow-up fetch of https://www.samsung.com/us/support/troubleshoot/TSG10004073/ before using these three records in production.

No official Samsung article was found that directly ties Safe Mode isolation to a gesture-direction complaint specifically (nav-007); this is an inferred application of a generally-verified technique (Safe Mode isolates third-party app conflicts) to the navigation-gesture domain, not a directly sourced fact.

No official Samsung source was found linking recurring overheating during light use directly to battery health/end-of-life (heat-009); this is sourced from a third-party repair guide (iFixit, S051), not Samsung support content.

perf-011 (clean reinstall after major OS update) is sourced entirely from a Samsung Community user discussion, not an official Samsung guide; no first-party Samsung article recommending a full reinstall-over-restore was located.

wifi-007 (disable Intelligent Wi-Fi) and wifi-008 (static IP) rely on community-reported menu paths; the referenced official article for wifi-008 (TSG01001559) was linked in a community post but not independently fetched and verified in this pass.

No deeplinks.json-equivalent catalog of masked bixby:// URIs was available in this research pass, so every record's deep_link field is intentionally null, consistent with the task's requirement to never fabricate deeplinks.

requires_human_review.note: Records with confidence='low', or whose only source was incompletely fetched. These should be reviewed against a fresh, full fetch of the cited source(s) before being trusted as verified Samsung guidance.

fabrication_safeguards_applied: No deep_link / bixby:// URI values were invented; every record's deep_link field is null.
No exact One UI version numbers were asserted unless a source explicitly stated device/version scope (see model_or_version_specific_records).
Where a source could not be fully fetched (S045, S046, S047), dependent records were marked confidence='low' and explicitly noted rather than presented as verified.
Community-forum and third-party-guide content was tagged with source_type != 'official_support' throughout, rather than being blended indistinguishably with Samsung's own documentation.

Synthetic query paraphrases were generated only as colloquial restatements of already-sourced canonical issues, kept in a separate top-level array (synthetic_query_variations) from the factual troubleshooting_records, and carry no invented troubleshooting steps of their own.
